reason: The text repeatedly depicts Yahweh as acting exclusively for the nation of Israel (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל - 'children of Israel') against Egypt. Key indicators include: (1) Yahweh commands Moses to tell Pharaoh 'send my people' (שַׁלַּח עַמִּי) and they will serve God; (2) Yahweh makes territorial distinctions protecting Israelite lands—Goshen is set apart so 'no swarms shall be there, that you may know that I am Yahweh in the midst of the land'; (3) Yahweh grants light to Israel's dwellings while darkness covers all Egypt; (4) The plagues are framed as divine intervention on behalf of Israel's national liberation. The statement 'there is none like Yahweh our God' (אֵין כַּיהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ) reinforces God's identity as Israel's national deity. Throughout this plague narrative, Yahweh's actions are directed entirely toward Israel's interests as a nation opposing Egypt.
